title: Can Browns start seriously thinking playoffs after latest comeback win over Texans?
content:
CLEVELAND — A stingy second-half defense and more late-game magic from Deshaun Watson helped the Cleveland Browns to a key 27-24 win over the Houston Texans on Sunday.

All six of the Browns’ wins this season have come thanks to game-winning drives in the fourth quarter. Watson did it again against Houston as the Browns overcame a 17-0 deficit. The winning drive was helped by an unnecessary roughness penalty on Texans cornerback Kamari Lassiter, but Watson’s 30-yard pass to Harold Fannin Jr. set up Quinshon Judkins’ 5-yard touchdown run with 53 seconds remaining.

C.J. Stroud and the Texans offense dazzled early on, scoring on the first three possessions. But the Browns defense did its part in response as Cleveland scored 20 straight points to take the lead into the fourth quarter.

The Browns’ defense got more pressure on Stroud after halftime and held him to 5-of-19 passing for 21 yards in the final two quarters. Houston had six three-and-outs on eight possessions in the second half and the Texans didn’t get a first down until the 10:53 mark in the fourth quarter.

The Texans did take a 24-20 lead off Stroud’s 11-yard touchdown pass to Dalton Schultz with 9:17 remaining. But Cleveland didn’t budge again for the rest of the afternoon, giving Watson one more shot to seal another win.

Watson finished 25-of-40 for 312 yards and an interception with a 6-yard touchdown run. Fannin had one of the game’s biggest catches and was the team’s leading receiver with seven catches for 91 yards.

The Browns are 4-0 at home for the first time since 1963. They are 6-2 in one-score games this season. The Browns are also the first team in NFL history to have its first six wins of a season all come by four points or fewer.

But most importantly, the Browns earned a win in what could be considered a pivotal game in the AFC playoff hunt. Cleveland heads into the bye while the Texans host the Indianapolis Colts next week.

The Browns blitzed more, and they actually got Stroud on the ground. The blitzes sped up Stroud in the pocket, and Cleveland also changed up some of its coverages to get Denzel Ward on Nico Collins. The Texans had some clear matchups they exploited early, but the Browns took those away. Browns linebacker Carson Schwesinger was seemingly everywhere and Ward was really good, too.

It’s everything. With a third-straight loss, the Browns would have been in big trouble and the Texans would have been on the charge. But now the Browns are 6-4, don’t play next week and return from their bye week with three straight at home. The Browns continue to overcome their slow starts and bad offensive stretches with fourth-quarter magic, and they’re now well positioned to be a playoff qualifier if their defense can hold up.

Today, Watson is going to have to share his game ball with the defense. But for all of the Browns’ faults and slow starts, they’ve been able to give Watson chances in these fourth quarters and Watson has continually found ways to deliver. The Browns were teetering in the fourth quarter and the Houston pass rush was continually getting home, but Watson again found the composure and found open receivers in the biggest moments.

The Browns made big plays. Watson was not consistently accurate, but he kept plays alive and continued to challenge the Houston defense. The Texans may have stepped off the gas, and they certainly got sloppy offensively. The Browns believe this can continue to happen, and they stayed alive to set up their sixth fourth-quarter win of the season. The Cleveland defense needed almost a quarter and half to come alive and the offense somehow saved enough energy for another final-drive victory. The Browns’ best play continues to involve just finding Fannin and letting him bulldoze would-be tacklers.
